newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB says to cut Dec long-term prime to 2.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: NCB says to cut Dec long-term prime to 2.5 pct.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) said on Tuesday that it was cutting its long-term prime lending rate for December to a record low of 2.5 percent from 2.7 percent in November.
The announcement follows a similar move announced on Monday by the Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd.
Meanwhile, NCB will cut the coupon rate of its five-year bank debentures to 2.15 percent from 2.25 percent for the November bank debentures, a spokesman for the bank said.
The change in the long-term prime rate will take effect from Wednesday.
The December bank debentures will be issued on December 27.
The difference in the coupon rate between NCB debentures and IBJ debentures will be 0.55 percent for the December debentures, compared with 0.45 percent previously.
IBJ set the coupon rate for its December bank debentures at 1.6 percent on Monday.
NCB's 2.25 percent November five-year bank debentures were tagged with a sell quote of 2.53 percent on Tuesday, a brokerage trader said.
Bank debentures are the major fund-raising tool of the three Japanese long-term credit banks. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk
